title: Bodycam
provenance: Reported by phmuni (highball-db#121, 2026-09-18): rated 3, playable with workarounds, Apple M5 (base), macOS 27.0, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r3, Highball 0.9.23, about 15 minutes played through Highball including online matches. Renderer not stated. Not run here.
notes: Unreal Engine 5 first-person shooter, Direct3D 12 only, so D3DMetal is the mode for it (from 0.9.26 Play picks it for Unreal 5 builds on its own). On a base M5 the one report gets about 40 to 50 fps on the training ground and around 30 fps online with every setting low, TSR at Quality, and the render resolution at half the display's native. Playable, but the reporter's own verdict is that a shooter at 30 to 40 fps is not the experience of better hardware. The game asks to install its Unreal prerequisites at every launch; agreeing to every prompt, including the ones labelled uninstall, lets it run (0.9.25 and later adopt runtimes a game installs, which may end the repeat prompts).

knownIssues.symptom: Asks to install UE prerequisites at every launch
knownIssues.cause: the game's prerequisite check does not see the runtimes as installed in the environment
knownIssues.fix: Agree to every prompt, including the ones labelled uninstall, and it runs; on 0.9.25 or later the environment adopts installed runtimes, which may stop the repeat prompts

knownIssues.symptom: Choosing any upscaler other than TSR or Off crashes the game, and afterwards it runs at 5 to 8 fps with the in-game menus locked, even after deleting the user config in AppData\Local
knownIssues.cause: not diagnosed; the non-TSR upscalers (reported on M5, macOS 27, engine r3) leave a broken state the config wipe alone does not clear
knownIssues.fix: Stay on TSR or Off. If it has already happened, uninstall the game, clear its AppData\Local files, and reinstall; the reporter says it can come back if those settings are changed again
